requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. The two newly metadata-safe diagnostic constructions produce exactly that location for metadata members, so MsgPack004/005 can now be reported without a location in the consuming project. That contradicts the new documentation and the recorded convention that such member diagnostics belong to the defining assembly; because MsgPack004 and MsgPack005 are errors, it can also break the consuming build.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a metadata library containing [MessagePackObject] generic struct Item<T> with a public property lacking [Key], then compile an app whose [MessagePackObject] has an Item<int> member and run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on the app. Assert that the app receives neither AD0001 nor MsgPack004 for Item<T>.Value. The changed !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource branch currently forwards the Location.None MsgPack004.

hunches.claim: The new location filter does not drop metadata-symbol diagnostics that have been converted to Location.None. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly with a public member lacking [Key], the null-safe MemberNeedsKey path creates MsgPack004 with a null location; !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is then true, so the consumer compilation receives a locationless MsgPack004 error. This both contradicts the helper's stated behavior and analyses metadata types that the defining assembly owns.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a Lib metadata reference containing [MessagePackObject] public partial struct Item<T> { public int Value { get; set; } } without running analyzers on Lib. Analyze an App compilation referencing Lib and containing [MessagePackObject] public class Cmd { [Key(0)] public Item<int> Member { get; set; } }. Assert that App has no MsgPack004, AD0001, or CS8785. On head, MsgPack004 is reported with Location.None instead of being dropped.

hunches.claim: One of the three reported crash sites remains unguarded: TypeCollector.cs:735 still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper cannot prevent this exception because it runs only after the diagnostic and its location have been constructed, so a metadata type reaching this diagnostic can still produce CS8785/AD0001.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a regression case using a closed generic struct from a metadata reference that reaches the diagnostic at TypeCollector.cs:735; assert that analyzer and generator execution complete without exceptions, CS8785, or AD0001. The case fails while DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] remains unguarded.

hunches.claim: The new tests do not exercise the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull crash path fixed at the former DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] access. All three metadata types have valid integer keys, so restoring the unguarded metadata-symbol access for this diagnostic would leave every added test passing.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1433 remove-guard: property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() -> property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax(); expected to survive because none of the added metadata-reference tests has a member whose key yields both a null int key and a null string key, so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull branch is never reached.

hunches.claim: The added tests only assert zero diagnostics and therefore cannot detect the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation predicate being inverted. That mutation would suppress ordinary diagnostics located in the compilation while all three new tests continued to pass.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) -> !(!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource || this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)); expected to survive because the added tests expect no in-compilation diagnostic and contain no positive case asserting that a local diagnostic is still reported.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Suppressing member diagnostics whose locations are outside the consuming compilation is deliberate behavior, not an unintended loss of diagnostics: referenced-assembly types are validated by their defining assembly. The wrapper and documentation implement that recorded convention.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed; the defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types, so missing diagnostics in the consuming assembly are not defects.
